bessere.en: better (comparative in front of a name)

texto: It is formed with **sich lassen** conjugated + infinitive at the end: **Das Problem lässt sich lösen** (the problem can be solved). The grammatical subject is the thing that can be done. In many contexts it is equivalent to **sein + zu + infinitivo**, but the record and nuance change.

It is a formal alternative to passive with modal. Depending on the context express obligation (**Die Rechnung ist sofort zu bezahlen**: you have to pay the invoice right away) or possibility (**Das Problem ist leicht zu lösen**: the problem can be easily solved). The verb conserves **zu** and goes to the end. It does not always amount to **sich lassen**: the first form appears much in formal instructions and texts.
In Präteritum: **Das ließ sich nicht vermeiden** (that could not be avoided). In Perfekt: **Das hat sich nicht vermeiden lassen**. In this construction with two infinitive, **haben** is used.

frases.de: Das Problem lässt sich bestimmt lösen.
frases.es: El problema seguro que se puede resolver.
frases.en: The problem is sure to be solved.

frases.de: Ich habe im Internet gesucht, aber die Seiten waren nicht hilfreich.
frases.es: He buscado en internet, pero las páginas no eran útiles.
frases.en: I looked on the Internet, but the pages were not useful.

frases.de: Das ließ sich nicht vermeiden, du musst bessere Quellen nehmen.
frases.es: No se podía evitar, tienes que usar mejores fuentes.
frases.en: You couldn't help it, you have to use better sources.

frases.de: Ich bezweifle, dass es eine einfache Lösung gibt.
frases.es: Dudo que haya una solución sencilla.
frases.en: I doubt there's a simple solution.

bloques.pregunta: What does «das lässt sich machen» mean?

opciones.texto: I command you to do that.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «could be avoided» (past)?

bloques.frase: Das ist unvermeidbar, das ___ sich nicht ändern.

opciones.explicacion: It is the form of «ihr»: it does not fit «das».
«ließ sich» is the «sich lassen» Präteritum indicating possibility in the past.

opciones.texto: He didn't want to avoid it in time.
opciones.explicacion: It does not express will («wollte»), but cannot be avoided.

opciones.texto: It was ordered to be avoided by court order.
opciones.explicacion: Without «sich», he would express an order or mandate to a third party.

bloques.pregunta: In a notice, what does «Die Rechnung ist sofort zu bezahlen» express?

opciones.texto: That you have to pay the bill right away.
opciones.explicacion: **sein + zu + infinitivo** expresses an obligation in this context.

opciones.texto: That the bill is already paid.
opciones.explicacion: That would be a result, not an obligation.

opciones.texto: That the bill can't be paid.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase does not express impossibility.

bloques.pregunta: How is it expressed with «sich lassen»: «That can be solved.»?

opciones.explicacion: The reflexive particle «sich» must accompany «lässt», not the final infinitive.
The construction requires infinitive («lösen»), not participle.

intro: The **sich lassen + infinitivo** construction expresses possibility: something can be done or resolved.
